content.title: STRATEGIC GOVERNANCE AND PARTNERSHIP MODELS FOR JUST ENERGY TRANSITIONS

content.text:
This chapter explores the critical role of governance and strategic partnerships in driving a just energy transition. It emphasizes the need for comprehensive, integrated approaches that address the social, economic, and environmental dimensions of the transition, ensuring no one is left behind.
Key themes include the importance of proactive planning, strategic foresight, and the transformation of physical infrastructure to enhance resilience and equity. The chapter also highlights the role of Just Energy Transition Partnerships (JETPs) as innovative financing mechanisms to support developing countries in shifting from fossil fuels to clean energy. Case studies, such as Zimbabwe’s employment impact modeling, illustrate how data-driven assessments and inclusive stakeholder engagement can inform effective policy development. The chapter underscores the necessity of transparency, equity, and international cooperation to achieve sustainable and just energy transitions.

lessons.title: Lesson 1: Governance Strategies for a Just Energy Transition
lessons.description: This lesson explores key energy governance strategies employed by UNDP, introduces the concept of energy democracy, and highlights practical examples.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Importance of Proactive Planning and Strategic Foresight
lessons.description: This lesson underscores the importance of proactive planning and strategic foresight in navigating the energy transition amid global crises like cost-of-living pressures and geopolitical instability. It highlights the need for collaborative governance and equitable infrastructure transformation to address historical inequities and build resilient systems

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Just Energy Transition Partnerships (JET-P)
lessons.description: This lesson explores Just Energy Transition Partnerships (JET-Ps) as innovative financing mechanisms to support developing nations in shifting from fossil fuels to clean energy. It emphasizes blending public and private capital to phase out coal, upgrade grids, and retrain workers. Challenges include ensuring equity, avoiding debt traps, and integrating grassroots priorities into national strategies. Effective governance and inclusive frameworks are stressed to balance economic shifts with social justice and accountability.
